original_question: Develop a theory of signed Hoffman graphs analogous to the Hoffman graph machinery used for unsigned graphs.
target_in_paper: Section 3.4, Problem 3.17: Extend the theory of Hoffman graphs to signed graphs.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper’s target as the open problem of creating a signed analogue of Hoffman graphs, and it also correctly captures that the intended comparison is with the Hoffman-graph machinery used in the unsigned setting.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is the narrower open problem “Extend the theory of Hoffman graphs to signed graphs,” stated in Section 3.4 as part of the smallest-eigenvalue program for signed graphs, rather than a broader request to develop arbitrary new signed-graph machinery.

To be stand-alone, the question should specify the ambient objects: a signed graph is Γ=(G,σ) with σ:E(G)→{+1,−1}, and the relevant operator is the signed adjacency matrix A(Γ), a real symmetric {0,+1,−1}-matrix.
The intended spectral parameter is the smallest adjacency eigenvalue λ_min(Γ); the draft does not state that the point of the extension is to study smallest-eigenvalue phenomena for signed graphs.

The nearby context matters: the problem appears immediately after discussion of graphs with λ_min≥−2, s-integrability, the hoped-for λ_min≥−3 extension, and maximal signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least −3; this situates the problem inside that specific smallest-eigenvalue framework.

The paper treats switching equivalence/switching isomorphism as the natural signed-graph equivalence, but the draft does not say whether the proposed signed Hoffman-graph theory should be formulated compatibly with switching.

No polynomial homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency hypothesis, or non-real coefficient field is involved here; the relevant linear-algebraic setting is real symmetric adjacency matrices, and the nearby integrability questions use integer matrices N satisfying s(A−⌊λ_min⌋I)=NN^T.
refined_question: Let Γ=(G,σ) be a signed graph, where σ:E(G)→{+1,−1}, and let λ_min(Γ) denote the smallest eigenvalue of its signed adjacency matrix A(Γ). Can one extend the Woo–Neumaier theory of Hoffman graphs to signed graphs so as to obtain an analogous structural tool for studying the smallest adjacency eigenvalue of signed graphs?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. In Section 3.4, after reviewing the unsigned classification for graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least −2 (Theorem 3.12), the signed-graph integrability analogue at the −2 threshold (Theorem 3.13), the proposed extension of the λ_min≥−3 integrability result (Problem 3.14), and the construction problem for maximal signed graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least −3 (Problem 3.16), the authors explicitly motivate Hoffman graphs as an essential tool for smallest-eigenvalue results in the unsigned setting and then pose Problem 3.17: “Extend the theory of Hoffman graphs to signed graphs.” So the faithful sharpening is to keep the question focused on a signed analogue of Hoffman graphs as a smallest-eigenvalue tool, not to broaden it beyond that nearby agenda.
